_note: Skyglass treasure hunts (push/268): the Drowned Foundry, the Quarantined Archive and the Captain's Watch, all HIDDEN, re-sent as whole-record edits. Change: a lost, drawn or fled fight now fails the hunt (fail_quest closes the isolated run; the chart was already spent at start). Before this, every loss reset to the fight's dialog, but an isolated pyramid keeps a defeated player in the run at 1 HP with no outside recovery (libs/combat/database.ts), so the retry could not be won (director 2026-10-25: 'failing a fight fails the quest'). Wins carry the player's pools into the next fight (the game default; no givePools). Also: the Captain's Purse pick is 100,000 ryo (was 50,000), and the Foundry and Watch premises no longer promise retries. Rewards, ladder, debuffs and proposals unchanged (see push/README 264-266). Generated by push/skyglass_hunts.gen.py; do not hand-edit.

data.name: The Drowned Foundry
data.description: Under the warship's keel are the works where the Core grows and pours the Skyglass that repairs the hull. The seawater got in when the ship fell, and the works kept running. The water rises the deeper you go, and the haul is at the bottom: there is no way out but through the crucible. Lose a fight and the works throw you out, chart and all.
data.successDescription: You carried the last pour out of the keel works.

objectives.description: Beneath the keel, seal channels feed a hatch rimmed with cooled crystal. Seawater pours past it into the dark. Somewhere below, something is still being poured.

nextObjectiveId.text: Climb down into the keel works

objectives.description: The intake is half flooded. A Deck Warden stands knee-deep in it, counting canisters that bob against the walls. 'No one is relieved,' he says, as if reading it from a list.
The Deck Warden and a Core Canister hold the intake.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description: Cooling racks line the first hall, stacked with fresh Skyglass that no one has collected. The water reaches your ankles and is still rising, and the hatch above has sealed behind you. A stair goes down into the pour halls.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go deeper into the pour halls

objectives.description: In the pour hall the Arsenal Keeper is checking the same ledger he has checked for decades, beside seal charges wired into every mould. He looks up. 'Unlisted personnel.'
The Arsenal Keeper sets off his charges.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description: The water is at your knees. The pour hall's best work sits on the moulds, and below it the crucible glows through the floor grates. Whatever runs the works is down there.

The crucible chamber is the only dry room in the works, kept dry by heat. The Foundry Warden stands in it, half fused with the pouring gear, a master smelter whose impression never set down his ladle. 'The last pour is not finished,' he says.
The Foundry Warden tips the crucible.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description: The Warden cools into a shell of crystal. The last pour sits unclaimed in its mould, and the works fall silent for the first time since the ship fell.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the last pour and leave

objectives.description: You carry the last pour out of the keel works. Above you the warship sails on, already starting to rebuild what you broke.
The flood takes you. You wash up on the shore below the wreck, and the chart is gone.

data.name: The Quarantined Archive
data.description: A chart marks a chamber missing from every ship plan. Someone aboard the Ghost Ship once tried to quarantine what the Core was getting wrong, and filed it behind three seals. A wrong answer at any seal trips the alarm: you fight the archive's guard, then continue. Answer all three cleanly for the better haul.
data.successDescription: The archive's last seal is broken and its records are yours.

objectives.description: The upward seal channels hold the ship aloft. A thinner line runs against their flow, carrying fragments of handwriting and fractured memories toward a sealed section inside the hull. Someone once tried to isolate a failure from the main network.

nextObjectiveId.text: Follow the breach into the hull

objectives.description: Below the waterline the hull is rebuilding itself from timber and cable that do not belong together. Something large is being rebuilt with them, and it is not finished.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face what the hull is building

objectives.description: The Core Horror pulls itself out of the frame.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description: With the Core Horror defeated, the surrounding frame begins sketching its ruined body again. Beneath the ladder, a severed impression conduit pulses toward a sealed maintenance chamber.

Rows of framed seal patterns stand without occupants. Each carries a human impression, not a living body: a remembered greeting, the shape of a hand reaching for warm tea, a command repeated until its meaning has faded. A small maintenance plate is locked behind the frames.
You choose: Force the Captain's command seal. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.
You choose: Override the lift lattice. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.

First seal. Three seal paths remain on the plate. One rises to the lift network, one bears the Captain's command mark, and a third turns back beneath the inactive frames. Beside the return path someone scratched: 'What command cannot repair must first be quarantined.'

nextObjectiveId.text: Trace the return seal beneath the frames

The alarm guard bars the way.

The shelf locks and the index burns white. The alarm guard comes for the archive itself.

objectives.description: The last seal opens a narrow chamber not marked on any ship plan. Command records and damaged crew impressions were moved here and filed as containment faults. Their custodian has not yet appeared.
The alarm dies as you cross into the archive, too late to matter. Command records and damaged crew impressions were filed here as containment faults. Their custodian already knows you are coming.

The reports span decades. Each warns that reconstructed patterns are deteriorating while preservation remains mandatory. The same seal-engineer's signature appears on every revision, although no living engineer could have filed them all. The final correction is stamped 'Access refused by command priority.'

A senior shinobi engineer gathers from the engraved lines, his form steadier than the damaged crew below. 'I sealed the worst of it away,' the Sealwright says. 'Command would not permit me to stop the work. It will not permit you to take these records.' He raises a sealing stance.
The Sealwright is waiting, already in his sealing stance. 'You came through my alarms,' he says. 'Then you know what this place is for.'
Break the Sealwright's containment defense.

objectives.description: Every seal held for you. You leave the archive with its records intact and its stores open, and the Sealwright's work unbroken.
The archive is yours, though the alarms cost you. You leave with what the custodian could not keep.
The archive's seals close over you. You are thrown out of the wreck, and the chart crumbles in your hand.

data.name: The Captain's Watch
data.description: The Captain's impression still keeps the night watch, and he never refuses a challenger. But the Oathkeeper sets terms: before each fight you may accept a handicap. Every term you take and survive raises the haul. Lose any fight and the watch is over.
data.successDescription: You kept the Captain's watch and claimed its stores.

objectives.description: The chart's route ends at a cove where the Ghost Ship's boat is drawn up on the sand, waiting. The Oathkeeper stands beside it. 'The Captain keeps the night watch,' he says. 'He will meet you. I set the terms.'
In the chart room the Wayfinder looks up from decades of corrections. The Oathkeeper speaks from the doorway: 'Fight him without your foreign seal-work, and the Captain will hear of it.'
You refuse the term. The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
Your seal-work goes quiet. The Wayfinder waits.
The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
